summary: A personal-narrative piece in the Neighborhood Stories series about Michaela Stephenson, a 42-year-old software engineer and mother of two, running her first full marathon at the annual City Marathon. It follows her pre-dawn training, mental doubts, family and community support, hitting the wall, and pain as a teacher, and draws broader lessons about perseverance and growth. Note that the article gives the race date as October 15th, 2023 but the finish as December 17th, 2023.
one_line: Michaela Stephenson, a 42-year-old mother and software engineer, runs her first City Marathon and finds lessons in perseverance, support, pain, and growth.
key_facts: Michaela Stephenson is a 42-year-old software engineer and mother of two who ran her first full marathon.
The annual City Marathon is described as starting on October 15th, 2023, with hundreds of runners at the starting line.
Michaela trained in September during early mornings while the world was quiet and her children slept.
Michaela said: "You discover that the body can take almost anything... It's your mind you have to convince."
Her support came from her spouse cheering her on, friends leaving encouraging notes, and her children chalking inspiring messages on the sidewalks.
On a long run on November 3rd, a stranger's cheer helped push Michaela forward when she was aching and nearly defeated.
When Michaela hit the wall, she faced a flood of forgotten misgivings, described as a millstone of doubt.
Michaela said each step beyond the wall felt like "an act of rebellion against the idea that my best days were behind me."
Michaela described pain as a teacher: "The pain was there to tell me that I was reaching new heights, marking a transition from who I was to who I could become."
In the final meters the crowd's roar swelled and her name was carried across the wind.
The article states Michaela crossed the finish line on December 17th, 2023, which conflicts with the October 15th, 2023 race date given at the start.
The piece concludes that life is a marathon, not a sprint, and that marathons are about philosophical revelations as well as physical conquest.
